info.title: mccontrol
info.description: The backend of mccontrol on 127.0.0.1: configuration, keys, the device directory, command sets, history, the command table and help, and the long-running verbs as jobs. JSON in and out, UTF-8. A job is started by POST /jobs/<verb> (202 with the job), followed by GET /jobs/<id> until its status is no longer running, and cancelled by DELETE /jobs/<id>. Every error is {"error": {"code", "message"}}; inside a job it is the job's error, with the same codes (broker and beacon for the network). Every route lives under the base URL serve() returns, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<secret>/, which is why the server entry is relative: a request outside it is a 404 with an empty body. Any route also answers 403 (forbidden) to a request whose Origin header is not the server's own, 415 (unsupported_media_type) to a body that is not application/json, 405 (method_not_allowed) to a method the path does not take, and 500 (internal) to a fault.

get.description: Parsed from what the device answered: the last answer to each read and every command's reply in its history, newest winning. `get <key>` answered `> value` is the fact `key`; `set <key> <value>` answered OK is the same fact; `ver` is `version`, `region` is `regions`, `get autoreply` gives `autoreply`, `autoreply.hops`, `autoreply.mode`, `autoreply.direct.flood`, `autoreply.private` and `autoreply.channel`. A read the table does not know is listed under `raw`.

cautions.description: With confirm_required only: each command that takes something away and what it takes

broker.description: the shared broker: every region without its own in `brokers` uses it

password_set.description: whether a broker password is set; the password itself is never returned

tested.description: the last connection test (POST /jobs/test): to which broker and port, whether every step passed, when

ui.description: the interface `mccontrol --ui` starts when none is named: the last one named; empty for none (Monolith then)

ui_settings.description: each interface's own preferences, by interface name then key, for it alone to read; {} when none is kept

brokers.description: each region's own broker, by IATA code (RB-1); a region not named here uses `broker`, the shared broker

registrations.description: when the key was registered with each broker, by host name

companion.description: your own companion radio for the mesh road: tcp:HOST:PORT, serial:PORT[:BAUD] or ble:ADDRESS; empty until set

mesh_after_mins.description: the auto road takes the mesh when a node has not been heard over MQTT for this many minutes (default 15, as the firmware's own auto)

Config.description: The control broker and how long to wait; command sets and shortcuts have their own routes.

password.description: set here, never returned: GET /config says password_set

ui_settings.description: merged into what is kept, interface by interface and key by key: an interface not named and a key not named stay as they are, a key given a value takes it, a key given null is deleted, and an interface left with no keys goes. Each interface's value must be an object, or the whole change is a 400

brokers.description: merged into the region -> broker map: a region given a host name uses that broker; one given null, "" or the shared broker's name goes back to the shared broker

companion.description: your own companion radio for the mesh road: tcp:HOST:PORT, serial:PORT[:BAUD] or ble:ADDRESS; empty until set

mesh_after_mins.description: the auto road takes the mesh when a node has not been heard over MQTT for this many minutes (default 15, as the firmware's own auto)

ConfigChange.description: Only the fields given change; an unknown field is a 400.

registered.description: the registration with the shared broker, as before RB-1

provision.description: the two serial lines that provision a repeater

registrations.description: every broker in use, the shared one first: when the key was registered there, or null

overwrite.description: replace an existing key: every node provisioned with it stops listening

seed.description: import this 64-hex seed instead of generating one

file.description: import a key file's text instead: a backup (mccontrol-key-backup, opened with passphrase) or a bare 64-hex seed

passphrase.description: the passphrase that opens `file` when it is a backup

node.description: the first 8 hex characters of the node's public key

key.description: the whole 64-hex key, known from ar-11 on

stale.description: sent to, and nothing heard for seven days

row.description: the directory row laid out to the asked width

broker.description: the broker this device is reached through: its region's own, or the shared broker

mesh_only.description: set by hand: the node has no Wi-Fi or MQTT and takes commands over the mesh alone; null: read from its version (an rc image without -observer)

last_heard_mqtt.description: the last answer that came over MQTT

last_heard_mesh.description: the last answer that came over the mesh

scheme.description: the plane the node speaks: mcc3 (its alive opened with your key, or lou-20 and later) or old (the per-node IATA scheme of lou-19 and older)

alive.description: the last alive message of this node that opened with your key: state, at, version, region (its region home), name, boot, sequence, last_counter, flags, old_scheme, relay (it relays for its owner) ...

counter.description: the last mcc3 counter sent to it

last_heard_relay.description: when the node last answered through a relay

forward_counter.description: as a relay: the counter of the last forward sent through it

relay_paths.description: per relay (its node id): the path from that relay to this node as its last answer taught it, {len, path, at}; the default for the next direct send through that relay

region.description: lou-19 and older: the IATA code; empty or '-' for lou-20 and later given by the whole key

mesh_only.description: true: mesh only (signed for meshcore/mesh/{KEY}/cmd, never sent over MQTT); false: not; null: from its version

key.description: the node's whole public key, 64 hex, starting with its id: the mesh road needs it

Adopt.description: A discovered node to remember; a taken name gets -2, -3 ...

forgot.description: the first 8 hex characters of the node's public key

verified.description: true: signed by the node; false: BAD SIGNATURE; null: unsigned, no answer, or a line from before this was kept

road.description: which road the command took; lines from before the mesh road are mqtt

relay.description: only for road relay: what the relay said of its forward

status.description: answered, no-answer (not a refusal: the node may have run the command), off, expired, replay, bad-body, busy, rate-limited, clock-unset, send-failed; null when the relay itself said nothing

sent.description: how the relay sent it; null when it sent nothing

snr.description: how the relay heard the answer, dB

verified.description: true: the node signed the answer; null: unsigned (an r1 from older firmware, Beacon's line, or kept before signatures were). A bad signature is never kept

key.description: the setting, as the firmware names it (txdelay, autoreply.hops), or version, regions

label.description: the key as a person reads it

at.description: when it was learned, local time

age.description: how long ago, short: now, 5 min, 2 h, 3 d

source.description: the command whose answer carried it

read.description: the command that reads it again

verified.description: true: the node signed the answer; null: unsigned (an r1 from older firmware, or kept before signatures were); a bad signature teaches nothing

facts.description: known settings first, in a fixed order, then the rest by key

raw.description: reads the fact table does not know, newest first

read.description: the reply is kept in the reads

probe.description: the sample the admission is judged on

admitted.description: does the device's firmware admit it; null with no device

needs.description: the oldest build that admits it

refusal.description: why the deny list refuses the probe; null when it travels

hidden.description: the device's image is built without the feature this command belongs to (lou-14: a trigger or an autoreply setting without auto-reply); not offered at all, unlike a greyed entry

revision.description: the revision the version reports, lou-N from lou-14 and ar-N before it; null when it reports none

features.description: the features the device's version names: ar, rc, arrc, ...; arrc for every version before lou-14; null without a device

lacks.description: ar or rc when the device's image is built without the feature the command needs; null otherwise or without a device

private_mismatch.description: for trigger private <key>: why no answer can come when the asking node and the target speak different private-test sub-types (0xF0 from lou-14, 0x04 before); null when they agree or a version is unknown

mesh_refusal.description: why the node would refuse the command over the mesh road (the repair allowance travels there; a mesh-only device refuses what needs an uplink); null when it travels

mesh_fits.description: whether the command fits the mesh road's 59 bytes

mesh_only.description: whether the device is mesh only; null without a device

example.caution: stops this repeater forwarding every message that carries no scope. It may be the only link between two places that rely on that.

TagChange.description: devices by name, node or unique prefix, and/or every device of a region

brokers.description: GET /regions only: the broker each region's devices use

Group.description: A named group of devices kept by mccontrol; a send to it is one signed per-node command to each member, never a broadcast.

GroupChange.description: devices by name, node or unique prefix

heard.description: the nodes heard so far in the current wait, as the transport reports them

cancellable.description: whether a cancel can interrupt this verb's waits: false for test and register, whose broker waits take no callback; discover stops listening and the regions left, but not the name read after a region

result.description: the verb's result; its schema is the operation's x-result-schema

group.description: a group's name: each member gets its own per-node command, in turn

region.description: an IATA code (lou-19 and older): each of your devices with that region, one per-node command each, in random order and spaced as for county; never a broadcast

confirm.description: required true for a command that takes something away (see /commands/check)

via.description: the road: mqtt (the default); mesh, through your companion (one node at a time, the command at most 59 bytes, the Wi-Fi and command-slot repair admitted); auto, the mesh for a mesh-only node, a command only the mesh admits, or a node not heard over MQTT for mesh_after_mins, else MQTT and the mesh if the broker cannot be reached, and MQTT again when the node answers mesh-closed; relay, a node of yours on MQTT (relay) transmits the mesh-road request and returns the answer: exactly one device, the mesh road's rules, never chosen by auto

relay.description: with via relay: the device that relays, by name or node id; it must be on MQTT and run lou-20 or later

route.description: with via relay: direct (along path), flood (in the relay's region home; a relay floods 2 an hour) or flood-wide (in the relay's default scope)

path.description: with via relay and route direct: the hops from the relay to the node as hex of one-byte hashes (2:HEX or 3:HEX for longer ones), or none; left out, the path the last answer taught this relay, else no hops

county.description: a county: each of your devices whose alive message names it as its region home (lou-20 and later), one sealed per-node command each, in random order, spaced 10-90 s (a restart 5-30 min)

SendJob.description: Exactly one target: devices, tagged (the tagged devices), group (its members, one by one), region (an IATA code) or county (a region home): every target is one per-node command per device, never a broadcast.

group.description: a group's name: each member gets its own per-node command, in turn

county.description: a county: each of your devices whose alive names it as region home, one after another

region.description: lou-19 and older only: JKG, several with commas, or * for every region you have; without it, your nodes from their alive messages (mcc3, lou-20 and later), wherever they are

add.description: remember every node not yet in the directory

TargetsJob.description: devices, or the tagged; neither means every device

region.description: the IATA region asked (old scheme); empty for a node found by its alive

broker.description: the broker the region was asked on

scheme.description: present for a node found by its alive message

state.description: from the alive scan: online (its alive opened), offline (its will cleared it), not-yours (it no longer opens with your key)

version.description: the firmware version its alive message carries

stats.description: Beacon's status block: battery_mv, uptime_secs, noise_floor, tx_air_secs, rx_air_secs, packets_sent, packets_received, errors, recv_errors, queue_len, internal_heap

sample.description: the latest Beacon status, null when Beacon has none

points.description: the telemetry buckets, oldest first; null when Beacon has none

registered.description: the registration with the broker tested

broker.description: the broker or brokers registered with, comma-separated

results.description: one per broker, in the order tried

command.description: a table entry text, as GET /commands lists it

values.description: the chosen choice, choices or typed value; empty ones are dropped

BrokerChoice.description: which broker: by host name (one in use), or the one a region uses; neither means the shared broker for a test and every broker in use for a registration

passphrase.description: at least 8 characters; the file opens with it, here or in the web app

KeyBackup.description: The seed sealed under a passphrase: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 then AES-256-GCM, the fields but `created` bound as additional data. The web app reads and writes the same file.

BadRequest.description: A malformed body or parameter, a command the node would refuse (refused), or a store refusal (store)

NotFound.description: No such route, device, set, topic or job

Conflict.description: The state forbids it: a key or a name exists (conflict), a command that takes something away was not confirmed (confirm_required), or the job has already finished (finished)
